case_studies.title: Substrate Asymmetry in User-Side Memory: A Diagnostic Framework
case_studies.abstract: User-side memory in LLMs is typically scored as a single "personalization" capability: given a user's history, is the output more user-aware? We show this aggregate metric hides opposite-direction failures. Memory factorises into at least three orthogonal axes -- behavioral consistency (style, voice), factual presence (recall facts in history), and factual absence (abstain when a fact is absent) -- and no single substrate wins all three. Comparing per-user gamma-LoRA (a small LoRA adapter trained on each user's history; gamma denotes per-user, not per-task) against BGE-large dense top-K retrie
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evaluating user-side memory in large language models by breaking it down into three orthogonal axes, creating a diagnostic framework to identify opposite-direction failures. The authors built a framework to compare different models, including gamma-LoRA and BGE-large dense top-K retriever. The result shows that no single model wins in all three axes, providing a more nuanced understanding of user-side memory.
case_studies.it_breakdown: Not directly applicable to IT infrastructure work, as it focuses on the development of large language models and their evaluation, rather than cloud infrastructure management.
case_studies.score_reasoning: The paper discusses a novel aspect of Large Language Model (LLM) memory, which is a key component of many AI applications used by IT engineers. It's a surprising finding that could raise interest among IT engineers using LLMs. The topic is highly relevant to IT engineers working with NLP and AI, and could potentially affect their work on model deployment and management. However, it may not be directly applicable to all IT engineers. The value of this research within 90 days is moderate, as it may help IT engineers understand and improve the performance of their LLMs. However, it is not directly actionable without further development and testing.

case_studies.title: Zero Touch Predictive Orchestration: Automating Time-Series Models for the Cloud-Edge Continuum
case_studies.abstract: The Cloud-Edge Continuum (CEC) enables latency-critical applications by distributing resources to the far edge, but its extreme volatility makes proactive Zero Touch Management via time-series forecasting essential. However, orchestrators face a severe "cold start" problem: newly discovered nodes lack the historical data required to train localized predictive models, while generalized models fail to capture unique hardware and microservice behaviors. To solve this, we propose a fully automated time-series prediction architecture driven by a novel data-mixing methodology. At the infrastructure
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of predicting resource demands in cloud-edge infrastructure, where the authors built an automated time-series prediction architecture, resulting in improved proactive management of resources. The architecture uses a novel data-mixing methodology to overcome the 'cold start' problem. This helps with efficient distribution of resources in latency-critical applications.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud-edge infrastructure, here is what to do: review your current forecasting models, consider implementing automated time-series prediction architectures, and evaluate the potential benefits of data-mixing methodologies for your specific use case. This flags a risk: if your org uses generalized predictive models, check for potential failures to capture unique hardware and microservice behaviors immediately. Apply this to optimize resource distribution and improve latency-critical application performance.
case_studies.relevance_tag: cloud infrastructure, edge computing, SaaS orchestration
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper discusses the Cloud-Edge Continuum, a concept directly relevant to IT infrastructure and edge computing. The automated time-series prediction architecture is an interesting approach to handling the 'cold start' problem. However, IT engineers are already dealing with infrastructure and cloud orchestration; novel AI maturity or monetization opportunities are not explicitly discussed. Value within 90 days will depend on the ability of IT engineers to utilize the proposed methodology for specific projects.

case_studies.title: Architecturally Significant MLOps Guidelines for ML Model Integration and Deployment: a Gray Literature Review
case_studies.abstract: Context. Despite the growing adoption of Machine Learning Operations (MLOps), teams often approach MLOps projects in an ad hoc manner due to the lack of consolidated architectural guidance. The community would benefit from a reference that synthesizes knowledge to inform the architectural design of MLOps systems, especially regarding the integration and deployment of ML models. Objective. In response, our goal is to provide a comprehensive overview of architecturally significant guidelines for the integration and deployment of ML models in MLOps systems. Method. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of lacking architectural guidance for Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) projects by providing a comprehensive overview of guidelines for integrating and deploying ML models. The authors built a reference guide by synthesizing existing knowledge from gray literature. The result is a set of architecturally significant guidelines for MLOps systems.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage MLOps systems, here is what to do: review the guidelines for integrating and deploying ML models, assess your current architecture against these guidelines, and update your design to ensure better model integration and deployment. This flags a risk: if your organization uses MLOps without a clear architectural design, check your model deployment process immediately to avoid potential issues.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Novelty: The paper synthesizes knowledge for MLOps systems, but this is a well-trodden area for IT engineers. IT Relevance: Addresses MLOps, integration and deployment of ML models. Value 90 days: Provides actionable guidelines for MLOps projects.

case_studies.title: Graph-Augmented Retrieval for Cross-Entity Financial Sentiment Analysis: A Comparative Study
case_studies.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become foundational for grounding large language models in domain-specific corpora, yet conventional vector-based RAG systems are fundamentally limited in their ability to capture the structured, multi-entity relationships that underpin financial market analysis. This paper presents a comprehensive comparative study of a novel two-hop Graph-RAG architecture versus a standard vector-only baseline for cross-entity financial sentiment analysis. Our system constructs a sentiment-weighted knowledge graph of 59 equity entities from 255 news articles covering
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of capturing complex relationships in financial market analysis by building a graph-augmented retrieval system for cross-entity financial sentiment analysis, resulting in a more comprehensive understanding of market trends. The system constructs a sentiment-weighted knowledge graph from news articles, improving upon conventional vector-based methods. This innovation enables more accurate financial sentiment analysis, but it's not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Automated Mediator for Human Negotiation: Pre-Mediation via a Structured LLM Pipeline
case_studies.abstract: Pre-mediation, the preparatory phase preceding direct human negotiation, plays a critical role in achieving mutually beneficial agreements, yet is often omitted due to cost, time, and limited access to trained mediators. We introduce an automated mediator for human negotiation, implemented as a structured pipeline of LLM modules, that supports pre-mediation in integrative negotiation settings. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of pre-mediation in human negotiation by building an automated mediator using a structured pipeline of LLM modules. The result is a system that supports effective preparation for human negotiation. This research is not relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Governed Capability Evolution: Lifecycle-Time Compatibility Checking and Rollback for AI-Component-Based Systems, with Embodied Agents as Case Study
case_studies.abstract: Software systems built from versioned AI components increasingly need lifecycle-time governance: when a capability module evolves into a new version, the hosting system must decide whether the new version may be activated safely, under what deployment conditions it should run, how it must be monitored, and when it should be rolled back. Existing software-deployment patterns (canary release, blue-green, feature flags, and MLOps pipelines) address parts of this loop but were designed for stateless web services rather than for stateful, policy-constrained runtimes that drive AI components in the
case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of safely updating AI components in complex systems by building a framework to check compatibility and roll back to previous versions if needed, resulting in more reliable AI-component-based systems. The researchers built a lifecycle-time compatibility checking and rollback system for AI-component-based systems. This research may impact IT work related to deploying and managing AI components in cloud infrastructure.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage AI-component-based systems in the cloud, here is what to do: review your current deployment patterns, assess whether they are suitable for stateful and policy-constrained AI runtimes, and consider implementing a compatibility checking and rollback system to ensure safe updates. This flags a risk: if your org uses AI components, check your deployment processes to ensure they can handle version updates safely. Not directly applicable to general IT infrastructure work, but relevant to those working with AI and machine learning systems.
case_studies.score_reasoning: Paper introduces concepts of lifecycle-time compatibility checking and rollback for AI-component-based systems, which may be relevant to IT infrastructure teams managing SaaS deployments, but novelty and real-world impact are moderate.
